message.content:
Here’s a mix of classics, modern hits, and hidden gems you can pick from:

| # | Title | Year | Why it’s worth watching |
|---|-------|------|--------------------------|
| 1 | **The Shining** (1980) | A masterclass in dread – slow‑burn tension, iconic imagery, and an unforgettable performance by Jack Nicholson. |
| 2 | **Hereditary** (2018) | A fresh take on family trauma turned supernatural nightmare; the score alone will keep you up at night. |
| 3 | **Midsommar** (2019) | If you want something bright but still terrifying, this daylight cult film turns pastoral beauty into pure dread. |
| 4 | **It Follows** (2014) | Simple premise, relentless pacing, and a creepy synth soundtrack make this indie gem feel like a new classic. |
| 5 | **The Babadook** (2014) | Psychological horror with a strong female lead; the monster is as much about grief as it is about fear. |
| 6 | **A Quiet Place** (2018) | Tension built around silence—every footstep feels like a death sentence. |
| 7 | **Get Out** (2017) | Satirical social commentary wrapped in a smart thriller; the twist is genuinely mind‑blowing. |
| 8 | **The Conjuring** (2013) | For those who love well‑crafted scares and a bit of paranormal lore. |
| 9 | **Suspiria** (1977) | Visually stunning, unsettling atmosphere, and a haunting score that lingers long after the credits roll. |
|10 | **The Witch** (2015) | Slow‑paced, period‑accurate dread that builds a sense of isolation and paranoia. |

Feel free to shuffle them or pair a classic with a newer film for contrast. Happy watching!
